design: Six executable primitives run twice in a privileged pod: baseline (stock utility path) and renamed-binary condition (utility copied to /tmp with a new name). Unique timestamped markers delimit 5 s windows. Actual Falco 0.45.2, Tetragon v1.7.1 and Tracee agents consumed the workloads.

Falco.alert_rule: Executing binary not part of base image
Falco.note: Renamed binaries are new files in the container upper layer, so a generic image-integrity rule fires. This is the opposite direction to the abstract interpreter, which treated TB-04 as a fragility (predicted rate drop from 92% to 80%).

Tetragon.note: Policies were loaded; process_exec/exit events for the scenario binaries were captured, but no path-specific kprobe/LSM event was attributable in this run. Not evidence that the tool cannot alert, only that this configuration did not.

Tracee.note: No configured event (security_file_open, cgroup_release_agent, core_pattern_modification) was attributable to the scenarios in this run.

interpretation: Engine-level calibration does not support the sign of the model's TB-04 prediction for Falco. Static anchor analysis identifies a dependency on binary identity, but the real engine's reaction to that dependency is to alert more, not less. The paper must not claim that renaming evades Falco; it can claim that the effect of renaming is engine- and rule-dependent, which motivates engine-level evaluation of static audit findings.
